what: This company owns and manages apartment buildings in large American cities. Its properties are concentrated in dense coastal and Sunbelt markets where renters are typically higher-income professionals.
customers: Apartment renters in major metropolitan areas, on leases typically of one year.
moat: Buildings in locations where new apartment supply is restricted by land scarcity and planning rules, so existing stock holds pricing power.
risks: New apartment supply in Sunbelt markets has held down rents
Debt of about $6 billion against almost no cash
Rent control rules in some of its markets limit increases
Property values fall when interest rates rise
opportunities: High mortgage rates keep would-be buyers renting for longer
Coastal markets have very little new supply under construction
A dividend yield above 4% backed by lease income
watch: Same-store rent growth and occupancy, and new supply in its markets.
